title: Towards An End-To-End Approach For Quantum Principal Component Analysis
journal_or_venue: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE)
abstract_summary: The paper presents an end-to-end implementation of quantum Principal Component Analysis (PCA), extending existing quantum state tomography methods to recover multiple eigenvectors including cases with complex amplitudes arising from non-integer eigenvalues. It provides a Qiskit-based implementation, analyzes complexity, and demonstrates the approach on a quantum finance use case (interest rate risk) with experiments on simulators and an IBM QPU, discussing limitations and scaling challenges.
methodology_description: The authors implement an end-to-end Quantum Principal Component Analysis (qPCA) pipeline in Qiskit: amplitude-encode a (normalized) covariance matrix A into a bipartite quantum state |psi_A> = sum_{i,j} A_{ij} |i>|j| = sum_k sigma_k |u_k>|u_k>, synthesize (precompute) the unitary approximation of e^{-iAt} (the paper uses precomputed operators rather than a qRAM-based exponentiation routine), and run Quantum Phase Estimation (QPE) with an eigenvalue register E to obtain the joint state sum_k sigma_k |lambda_k>_E |u_k>|u_k>. To extract classical principal components they extend prior tomography methods to handle complex amplitudes via a two-stage tomography: (1) Probability estimation by repeated measurements (frequentist counts) to estimate |amplitudes| = sqrt(p_i), and (2) Sign estimation using a controlled-Hadamard-test-like circuit that prepares (1/sqrt{2})(|0>|x> + |1>|p>) with U_x (preparation of eigenvector state) and U_p (preparation of sqrt-probability state) controlled by an ancilla; measuring the ancilla and targets yields sign information for components. Eigenvalues are reconstructed by aggregating counts on the E register (using r_PE qubits for resolution), locating the top local maxima, and factoring out coefficients from register M to recover eigenvectors. The implementation uses Qiskit StatePreparation and PhaseEstimation classes; the unitary e^{-iAt} used in QPE is precomputed in code. The authors analyze space/time complexity (dominated by Hamiltonian simulation cost O(t^2/epsilon) copies of A for e^{-iAt}), and validate the method on a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix (derived from 1000 simulated returns per asset), using IBM’s qasm simulator and the IBM Perth QPU for experiments.
experimental_setup: Ideal simulations on IBM's qasm simulator (ibmq_qasm_simulator). Real-hardware runs on IBM Perth QPU (7 qubits, quantum volume 32). Experiments used r_PE = 2 (2 qubits for eigenvalue register), Nc = 50000 measurement shots for tomography. Amplitude-estimation circuit used 4 qubits total (2 for M, 2 for E); sign-estimation circuit used 5 qubits (an additional control qubit). The e^{-iAt} unitary was precomputed and supplied to the PhaseEstimation primitive.
dataset_used: Synthetic financial data representing a 2x2 covariance matrix of two hypothetical assets. The matrix A = [[0.6507, 0.2122], [0.2122, 0.3493]] was constructed from simulations of 1000 return scenarios per asset over one year; the resulting covariance was used as input (trace-normalized in the example).
experiment_input: Synthetic two-asset returns simulated (1000 scenarios per asset, one-year horizon). Covariance matrix computed from simulated returns producing A (2x2). Preprocessing: compute covariance; normalize by trace if required for amplitude encoding; load amplitudes using Qiskit's StatePreparation (no qRAM used). The e^{-iAt} operator was precomputed and supplied to PhaseEstimation.
experiment_process: 1) Prepare amplitude-encoded state |psi_A> for matrix A using Qiskit StatePreparation. 2) Precompute the unitary e^{-iAt} (operator provided to the circuit). 3) Run Quantum Phase Estimation with r_PE qubits (r_PE=2 in experiments) to obtain joint eigenvalue/eigenvector superposition. 4) Probability estimation: measure M+E registers Nc times (Nc=50000) to estimate probabilities p_i and derive |amplitudes| = sqrt(p_i). 5) Sign estimation: build controlled circuit with an ancilla; conditionally apply U_x (preparation of the eigenvector state) and U_p (preparation of sqrt-probability state); apply Hadamard on ancilla and measure to infer signs of amplitudes using thresholding rules. 6) Aggregate counts on eigenvalue register to identify eigenvalues (peak finding over r_PE-bit outcomes). 7) Extract eigenvectors from register M (factoring out coefficients) to reconstruct principal components. 8) Compare results from ideal simulator and IBM Perth QPU; note degraded performance on QPU sign estimation due to noise/decoherence.
experiment_output: Outputs comprised measurement count histograms and aggregated probabilities for eigenvalue register outcomes, reconstructed eigenvalue estimates (with resolution 1/2^{r_PE}) and reconstructed eigenvectors (component amplitudes with inferred signs). Results were compared qualitatively to the analytical eigen-decomposition (λ1=0.760, u1=[0.889, 0.459]; λ2=0.240, u2=[-0.459, 0.889]). No explicit numerical error metrics (e.g., fidelity or MSE) were reported; outputs were presented as counts/probability plots and reconstructed vectors. Simulator matched expected outputs; QPU showed amplitude results close but sign-estimation degraded due to noise.

reproducibility_notes: Code repository made available by authors: https://github.com/Eagle-quantum/QuPCA. Synthetic dataset construction (1000 simulated returns per asset) and the 2x2 covariance matrix are described in the paper; the unitary e^{-iAt} was precomputed in code and not generated via a qRAM or automatic Hamiltonian simulation routine, which is noted as a limitation for scaling. The implementation uses Qiskit primitives (StatePreparation, PhaseEstimation); reproducing larger instances requires providing the same precomputed unitary and substantial classical precomputation. Experiments on real hardware are subject to device noise (not mitigated), which affected sign-estimation results.

[supported] They extended an existing quantum state tomography procedure to reconstruct eigenvectors from the phase-estimation output, and implemented a two-step tomography (probability estimation + sign estimation).

[speculative] The tomography extension is claimed to handle complex amplitudes arising from non-integer eigenvalues by assuming the imaginary components become negligible with sufficiently high eigenvalue resolution.
[supported] Ideal-simulator experiments on a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix produced the expected amplitude-estimation results and reconstructed eigenvalue peaks consistent with the target matrix.

[supported] Sign-estimation (Hadamard-test-like) worked in ideal simulation but suffered on real hardware: amplitude estimation remained reasonably close on IBM Perth QPU but the deeper sign-estimation circuit was degraded by noise/decoherence.

[speculative] The paper presents a complexity analysis showing the algorithmic cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation (density matrix exponentiation), quoted as O(t^2 ε^{-1} log(N^2)) copies/time for e^{-iAt} preparation under the low-rank assumption.

[supported] Because they did not implement qRAM, the implementation uses Qiskit's StatePreparation for data loading (i.e., a classical precomputation approach rather than a scalable qRAM-based loader).

[speculative] The authors note (and claim) that demonstrating quantum advantage would require scalable/efficient data loading, improved Hamiltonian simulation, and error mitigation — scaling up requires more quantum resources and error-correction/mitigation techniques.

[speculative] The paper reiterates literature claims of an exponential advantage for quantum PCA under certain assumptions (multiple copies of the density matrix and efficient e^{-iAt}), but does not experimentally demonstrate such an advantage.

results_summary: The paper presents a practical Qiskit implementation of quantum PCA up to eigenvector extraction, including an extended tomography procedure to handle complex amplitudes. The authors validate the approach on a small 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix: ideal-simulator runs reproduced expected amplitude- and sign-estimation behavior and identified eigenvalue peaks; experiments on a 7-qubit IBM device (Perth) showed reasonable amplitude estimation but sign estimation failed due to circuit depth and noise. The implementation uses StatePreparation rather than qRAM for data loading. A complexity analysis highlights that Hamiltonian simulation (density matrix exponentiation) dominates runtime under the low-rank assumption. The work supplies code and documents practical limits and assumptions (notably the need for high eigenvalue resolution and improved data-loading and error-mitigation techniques for scaling).

quantum_advantage_detail: The paper cites prior work that claims an exponential advantage for quantum PCA under assumptions (access to multiple copies of the density matrix and efficient density-matrix exponentiation). However, the authors do not demonstrate an advantage experimentally: they use precomputed unitaries in Qiskit rather than scalable qRAM or an implemented density-matrix exponentiation, and their experiments are small-scale (2x2) with noisy real-device results degrading deeper circuits. Thus any claimed advantage remains theoretical in this work.
limitations: Quantum PCA still lacks a complete end-to-end algorithmic implementation (author-stated).
The tomography step for extracting principal components is challenging, especially when output states have complex amplitudes (author-stated).
Some efficient quantum PCA implementations cannot handle matrices with non-integer eigenvalues (author-stated).
No Qiskit (or other SDK) implementation of the e^{-iAt} construction proposed in the literature was available to the authors; in code they precompute the operator (author-stated).
The presented implementation relies on ad-hoc StatePreparation (Qiskit) for data loading rather than qRAM; this is a placeholder and does not scale (author-stated).
Phase estimation requires sufficiently high resolution (more qubits) to keep imaginary parts negligible; choosing resolution is critical (author-stated).
Sign-estimation tomography assumes the imaginary component of amplitudes is small and approximates it to zero — this approximation can fail if resolution is insufficient (author-stated).
Tomography requires a large number of shots/copies (Nc = O(36 d ln d / δ^2)) which grows with state dimension and target error (author-stated).
Hamiltonian simulation (e^{-iAt}) for low-rank A needs many copies of A: O(t^2 ε^{-1}), which dominates time complexity and resource needs (author-stated).
Experimental validation is limited: experiments are small-scale (2×2 covariance matrix) and mostly run on ideal simulator; limited real-QPU results (author-stated).
Real-QPU experiments (sign circuit) suffered from decoherence and noise due to increased circuit depth; performance degraded relative to ideal simulation (author-stated).

key_ideas: #idea:hybrid-approach — Implemented an end-to-end qPCA pipeline in Qiskit that relies on classical precomputation of the e^{-iAt} unitary and classical postprocessing (tomography/peak finding) to extract principal components.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Demonstrated the method on a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix using both an ideal simulator and IBM Perth QPU (real-hardware); simulator matches analytics, QPU shows degraded sign estimation due to noise.
#limitation:qubit-count — Experiments limited to 4–5 qubits for amplitude/sign circuits and 2-qubit eigenvalue register (r_PE=2), demonstrating very small-scale applicability.
#limitation:noise — Real-device sign-estimation performance degraded by decoherence/noise; no advanced error mitigation applied.

#limitation:data-encoding — Amplitude-encoding/state-preparation used (Qiskit StatePreparation) and the e^{-iAt} operator was precomputed classically rather than produced via scalable qRAM/Hamiltonian simulation, highlighting data-loading and precomputation bottlenecks.
contradictions: The paper frames an "end-to-end" quantum PCA pipeline but relies on a classically precomputed e^{-iAt} unitary supplied to PhaseEstimation; this reliance undermines the claim of a fully quantum end-to-end workflow (contradiction between claimed end-to-end quantum processing and classical precomputation).

The implementation demonstrates feasibility on a 2x2 problem with r_PE=2, yet the authors' own complexity analysis highlights Hamiltonian simulation costs (O(t^2/epsilon)) and the need for many copies of A, contradicting any implication that the approach currently scales to realistic financial covariance sizes without significant classical resources or advanced Hamiltonian simulation/qRAM.
